title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff tasted New England clam chowder and Dunkin' Munchkins on stage in Mansfield, Massachusetts.
Duff expressed apprehension about trying clam chowder but enjoyed the base and broth after tasting.
The singer added local food tastings, including chicken in Nashville and pizza in New York, to her concert tour.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman is set to make his Red Sox debut on Tuesday against the Blue Jays in Toronto.
Rutschman was acquired from the Orioles and has been recovering from wrist inflammation since July 18.
Red Sox may adjust their roster, possibly affecting Connor Wong or Jake Rogers, to accommodate Rutschman's activation.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Springfield's The Zoo in Forest Park remains closed after severe thunderstorms and intense winds caused massive damage.
Though no animals were injured, the storm uprooted trees and destroyed enclosures, prompting a state of emergency in Springfield.
The zoo faces financial challenges from lost revenue and repair costs, with donations being accepted online.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough Monday afternoon.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East was closed following the crash, causing traffic delays.
Authorities advise drivers to seek alternate routes and expect heavier traffic near the crash site.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Shrewsbury police were alerted to a possible drowning at Lake Quinsigamond near Sunset Beach on Sunday afternoon.
Search efforts using divers and drones were conducted, but the man's body wasn't found until Monday morning.
A dive team located the male victim using sonar technology; the cause of the drowning is under investigation.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Undrafted linebacker Khalil Jacobs is making a strong impression at Patriots training camp, aiming for a roster spot.
Jacobs, the former University of Missouri player, was signed by Patriots as an undrafted free agent in May 2026.
During camp, Jacobs has shown versatility and speed, contributing significantly in scrimmages and practice sessions.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed H.5595, expanding abortion rights by removing gestational limits in Massachusetts.
The law allows abortions post-24 weeks based on physician judgment, reducing out-of-state travel for care.
Opponents argue the legislation weakens protections for unborn children, while supporters say it enhances healthcare access.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of Sebastian, a free Black man who died in 1729, was restored and reinstalled in Boston's Granary Burying Ground.
Discovered during a conservation project, it is believed to be the oldest gravestone of a free Black person in the United States.
Sebastian, also known as Boston, previously enslaved, campaigned for marriage rights and inspired early antislavery movements in Massachusetts.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to Patriots practice, while Charles Woods and Christian Barmore remained absent.
Romeo Doubs impressed with a highlight catch in end zone; Kyle Williams also made a deep catch during practice.
Patriots to resume full-pad practices Tuesday against Colts, gearing up for the preseason opener on Thursday.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard at Scarborough Beach, Maine, was briefly dragged underwater by a white shark on Saturday.
The beach was closed for an hour as officials assessed the situation and monitored surrounding waters.
Scarborough officials reported increased white shark activity near Scarborough Beach State Park and Higgins Beach.
